decisions.rationale: Accepted independently on exact commit 843af270bed5d8d89201865a5484b43b35f80488. Trigger: parseRules uses startsWith("@media") and mediaQueries permits no token boundary, so the unknown at-rule @mediascreen is classified as @media. Mask: both source-reader paths normalize the same malformed prefix and task 6 renders only at 400px, where the base layout is expected. Learner-visible symptom: the public command reports 7 pass/0 fail even though Chromium keeps one card column at 600/700/1100px and keeps .page display:block at 1000/1100px. Changing only the malformed prefix to the valid '@media screen and' spelling makes public and browser results agree. Correct the at-keyword check narrowly: recognize media exactly, ASCII case-insensitively, with a valid boundary; add an @mediascreen negative regression and 700/1100px browser assertions. Preserve rejection of wrong direction, strict boundary, wrong threshold, wrong unit, compound, print, malformed-condition, and out-of-order queries, and do not disclose a completed learner rule.

Accepted independently on exact commit 843af270bed5d8d89201865a5484b43b35f80488. Trigger: media-rule discovery is case-sensitive and breakpoint identity/order are compared as integer source strings instead of numeric px dimensions. Mask: Chromium applies both valid spellings, while tasks 1-3 and the 400px-only task 6 do not exercise the wider breakpoints. Learner-visible symptom: both @MEDIA and exact 600.0px/1000.0px solutions report 4 pass/3 fail although Chromium changes to two card columns at exactly 600px and to the page grid at exactly 1000px. Canonical lowercase integer spelling passes; the disconfirming 600.5px route correctly remains one column at 600px and fails the public breakpoint check. Correct only the supported lab grammar: compare the media at-keyword ASCII case-insensitively and parse finite decimal px dimensions numerically for exact 600/1000 equality. Add passing @MEDIA and decimal-equivalence regressions while retaining every existing invalid-direction, strict-boundary, threshold, unit, media-type, compound, malformed, and ordering rejection.

Accepted independently on exact commit 843af270bed5d8d89201865a5484b43b35f80488. The learner contract asks for one card column on phones and two equal columns from 600px, says learners decide which Grid and media-query rules produce the outcome, and does not prohibit custom properties. Trigger: task 4 compares unresolved var() source text with a direct-value allowlist; cleanValue also rewrites commas inside quoted custom-property tokens. Mask: the only existing browser assertion runs at 400px and checks overflow/hero fit, not card columns. Learner-visible symptom: a defined --one-column/--two-columns route renders one column at 599px and two at 600/700px but reports 6 pass/1 fail; the reader changes a quoted "a,b" token to "a, b". Replacing var() with its direct values passes, while missing variables at both widths leave one rendered column at 600px and correctly fail. Do not widen the dependency-free reader into a general CSS parser: validate the relevant computed card outcome with the already pinned Chromium at 599px and 600px, retain narrow source checks for Grid and increasing mobile-first media rules, and avoid normalizing custom-property/string token contents. Add passing indirection and quoted-token regressions plus a failing unresolved-variable regression; preserve outcome-first feedback and no solution disclosure.
